key_insight: The models project global solar PV costs falling to about 8 USD/MWh by 2050, while onshore wind reaches about 43 USD/MWh and approaches a 35 USD/MWh floor.
engineering_relevance: National renewable-energy planning should account for technology-specific cost trends, local capacity factors, capital costs, and financing conditions rather than relying solely on global averages.
method: Curate a comprehensive database of national solar PV and onshore wind costs.
Decompose national levelized electricity costs and model each component separately.
Predict national deviations from global costs and compare forecasts with integrated assessment model projections.
evidence_signal: Historical analysis finds solar module and balance-of-system costs declining roughly 12% annually since 1990, versus 4% for wind turbines and no decline in wind balance-of-system costs.
watch_item: The 2050 estimates depend on modeled cost trends; this is renewable-cost forecasting research, not an AI-driven solar-cell design study.
paper_title: Will national renewable costs continue declining?
